title: Dead Drop
summary: Suspicious DNS queries are hiding data in plain sight. Decode the payload.
briefing:
NebulaCorp's edge DNS resolver logged a burst of unusual queries. Normal internal traffic queries known corporate domains, but a handful of queries resolve subdomains of "exfil.nebula.test" — a domain that does not exist in the corporate zone.

The subdomain labels look like hex-encoded data. If someone is tunnelling information out through DNS, the payload is in those labels.

Extract every query to *.exfil.nebula.test, concatenate the subdomain labels (the part before ".exfil.nebula.test") in chronological order, and decode the hex to recover the hidden message.

The decoded message is a flag. Submit it exactly as it appears.
objectives: Filter the DNS log for queries to *.exfil.nebula.test
Concatenate them in timestamp order and decode from hex

hints.title: Filter pattern
hints.text: grep "exfil.nebula.test" dns-queries.log isolates the suspicious queries. The subdomain label is the first dot-separated segment of the query name.

hints.title: Decode method
hints.text: After extracting the hex labels, concatenate them into one string and run: echo "<hex>" | xxd -r -p
